data.body:
[P1] Skip nonterminal gaps once completion is known

With `maxConcurrency: 3`, default fail-fast, and resumed item states `[FAILED, SUCCEEDED, SUCCEEDED, STARTED, SUCCEEDED]`, let item 0's cached failure settle first. Reconciliation still calls `tryStartNext()`, which launches unfinished item 3 because its index is below `lastRecorded`. This history is reachable: items 1 and 2 finish and start items 3 and 4; item 4 finishes, then item 0 fails. The base implementation stops on the cached failure without resuming item 3. This change can instead execute new durable steps and external side effects in item 3 after failure is already known, especially while cached successes deserialize slowly. Limiting scheduling to the last recorded index does not protect gaps. Once a completion condition fires, advance/reserve child IDs for nonterminal gaps without executing them, while continuing to recover terminal records. Add a regression with a STARTED gap and held cached deserialization.
